JIRA_CREATE_ISSUE.title: CreateIssueRequest

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: List of labels to categorize the issue; new labels are created if they don't exist.
labels.human_parameter_description: Tags to help categorize and find this issue later. Add one or more labels like bug, customer, or release-2.3.

parent.title: Parent
parent.description: Parent issue key (e.g., 'PROJ-123') or issue ID. IMPORTANT: This field should ONLY be used when creating sub-task issue types (e.g., 'Sub-task', 'Subtask'). It is required for sub-tasks. Jira enforces strict hierarchy rules: standard issue types (Task, Story, Bug) can ONLY have Sub-tasks as children, not other standard issues. Epics can have Stories/Tasks/Bugs as children. Attempting to set a parent on a non-sub-task issue type or using an incompatible parent-child combination will result in a hierarchy error. The parent must be an existing issue in the same project. NOTE: Alternative field names 'parent_key' and 'parent_id' are also accepted and will be automatically mapped to this field.
parent.human_parameter_description: The key or ID of the parent issue when creating a sub-task. This should ONLY be used for sub-task issue types. Standard issues like Task, Story, or Bug cannot have other standard issues as children - they can only have Sub-tasks as children. You can also use 'parent_key' or 'parent_id' as alternative names for this field.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: REQUIRED. Brief, descriptive title for the issue. This is the main headline that will appear in Jira (e.g., 'Fix login button not working', 'Add user profile page').
summary.human_parameter_description: A short, clear title for the issue so teammates can quickly understand what it's about. Keep it concise and descriptive.

assignee.title: Assignee
assignee.description: Account ID of the user to assign the issue to. Must be a valid Jira account ID in one of these formats: (1) Cloud format with tenant ID and UUID: '712020:xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx', or (2) Legacy 24-character hex string: '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'. IMPORTANT: Do NOT pass email addresses here - use assignee_name field for emails. The account ID is validated to ensure the user exists and can be assigned to issues in the target project. Use JIRA_FIND_USERS to get valid account IDs. Takes precedence over assignee_name if both are provided. NOTE: Some Jira projects (especially Jira Service Management/Service Desk projects) may not allow setting the assignee at issue creation time because the field isn't on the project's create screen. If this occurs, the issue will be created successfully without the assignee, and you'll need to set the assignee separately using JIRA_ASSIGN_ISSUE after creation.
assignee.human_parameter_description: The Jira account ID (not email) of the person who should work on this issue. Must be a valid account ID format. To assign by email, use the Assignee Name field instead. Use JIRA_FIND_USERS to find valid account IDs. This will override Assignee Name if both are provided. Note: Some projects may not allow setting assignee at creation time - use JIRA_ASSIGN_ISSUE to set it after creation if needed.

due_date.title: Due Date
due_date.description: Expected resolution date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
due_date.human_parameter_description: When you expect this issue to be completed. Use the date format YYYY-MM-DD.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Priority level for the issue. Can be either a priority name or a valid priority ID from the Jira instance. IMPORTANT: Priority names are completely instance-specific and vary by Jira configuration (e.g., some instances use 'Highest'/'High'/'Medium'/'Low'/'Lowest', while others use 'P0'/'P1'/'P2'/'P3'/'P4', or custom names). It is strongly recommended to either: (1) check available priorities for your instance first using JIRA_GET_ISSUE_EDIT_META or by inspecting existing issues, or (2) omit this field if unsure. When the global priority endpoint is available, the value is validated against available priorities. If validation is unavailable (404), the value is passed through to Jira for validation.
priority.human_parameter_description: How urgent or important the issue is. IMPORTANT: Priority names vary by Jira instance and are NOT universal - what works in one instance may not work in another. Some instances use names like 'High'/'Medium'/'Low', others use 'P0'/'P1'/'P2', and some have custom priority names. It's recommended to check available priorities for your specific Jira instance first, or use priority IDs (like '1', '2', '3') which are more reliable. If unsure, it's safer to omit this field.

reporter.title: Reporter
reporter.description: Account ID of the user reporting the issue. Defaults to the API request user if unspecified.
reporter.human_parameter_description: The Jira account ID of the person reporting or creating the issue. Leave blank to use your own account.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: List of IDs for versions affected by this issue; versions must exist in the project.
versions.human_parameter_description: Which product versions are impacted by this issue. Provide version IDs that already exist in your project.

sprint_id.title: Sprint Id
sprint_id.description: ID of the sprint to assign this issue to. The issue will be added to the specified sprint if provided.
sprint_id.human_parameter_description: The sprint to add this issue to. Enter the sprint's numeric ID from your board.

components.title: Components
components.description: List of component IDs (e.g., '10000'); components must already exist in the project.
components.human_parameter_description: The project components this issue relates to. Enter existing component IDs from your project.

issue_type.title: Issue Type
issue_type.description: REQUIRED. Type of the issue - must be valid for the target project as available types vary by project configuration. CRITICAL: Always use JIRA_GET_ISSUE_TYPES to check valid types for your project BEFORE creating issues. Can be either a type name (e.g., 'Task', 'Story', 'Epic') or type ID (e.g., '10001'). Common types include Task, Story, Epic, and Bug, but NOT ALL projects support all types. Issue type names are localized based on your Jira instance's language settings (e.g., 'Task' in English, 'Задача' in Russian, 'Tâche' in French). Using the issue type ID is language-independent and more reliable.
issue_type.human_parameter_description: The type of issue to create (e.g., Task, Story, Epic). This is REQUIRED - there is no default value. IMPORTANT: Available issue types vary by project. Always use JIRA_GET_ISSUE_TYPES to check valid types for your specific project before attempting to create an issue, or use the type ID for language-independent operation.

description.title: Description
examples: Login page is not working when clicking submit button after entering valid credentials.
**Critical Bug**: The `user.login()` method fails when processing valid credentials. See [documentation](https://docs.example.com) for details.
description.description: Detailed description of the issue. Accepts either: (1) A plain text or Markdown string (converted to ADF internally), or (2) A pre-formatted Atlassian Document Format (ADF) dict with keys 'type'='doc', 'version'=1, and 'content' array. description.human_parameter_description: The full details of the issue, such as steps to reproduce, expected vs. actual results, and any context. You can format it with Markdown for readability, or pass a pre-formatted ADF object.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Environment details. Accepts either: (1) A plain text or Markdown string (converted to ADF internally), or (2) A pre-formatted Atlassian Document Format (ADF) dict with keys 'type'='doc', 'version'=1, and 'content' array. When passing ADF directly, formatting is preserved as-is.
environment.human_parameter_description: Details about where the problem occurs, such as production or staging, app version, browser, or OS. This helps others reproduce and investigate the issue. You can pass Markdown text or a pre-formatted ADF object.

project_key.title: Project Key
project_key.description: REQUIRED. Key of the Jira project where the issue will be created (e.g., 'KAN', 'DEV', 'PROJ'). This is the short uppercase code that appears in issue keys like 'PROJ-123'. Must be an existing project key in your Jira instance. Use JIRA_GET_ALL_PROJECTS to list available projects if you don't know the key.
project_key.human_parameter_description: The short code of the Jira project where you want to create the issue (for example, KAN). You can find it in your project's key or in issue keys like KAN-123. Use JIRA_GET_ALL_PROJECTS to list available projects.

fix_versions.title: Fix Versions
fix_versions.description: List of IDs for versions where the issue is/will be fixed; versions must exist in the project.
fix_versions.human_parameter_description: Which versions you plan to deliver the fix in. Provide version IDs that exist in your project.

assignee_name.title: Assignee Name
assignee_name.description: Name or email of the user to assign the issue to. Can be either an email address (e.g., 'john@company.com') or display name (e.g., 'John Doe'). The system will auto-detect the type and search accordingly. Ignored if assignee (account ID) is also provided. NOTE: Slack user IDs (e.g., 'U02QWF25EQ6') are not supported - use the Jira user's email, display name, or account ID instead. NOTE: Some Jira projects (especially Jira Service Management/Service Desk projects) may not allow setting the assignee at issue creation time because the field isn't on the project's create screen. If this occurs, the issue will be created successfully without the assignee, and you'll need to set the assignee separately using JIRA_ASSIGN_ISSUE after creation.
assignee_name.human_parameter_description: The name or email of the person to assign the issue to if you don't know their account ID. We'll look up the correct user based on what you enter. Note: Slack user IDs are not supported. Some projects may not allow setting assignee at creation time - use JIRA_ASSIGN_ISSUE to set it after creation if needed.

Use this for custom fields or any fields not covered by the standard parameters (e.g., Story Points, custom text fields, etc.). Format: '{"customfield_10104": 5, "customfield_10200": "value"}'. Rich text custom fields (textarea type) accept plain text or Markdown - they are automatically converted to Atlassian Document Format (ADF). You can also pass ADF directly as a JSON object. Use JIRA_GET_CREATE_METADATA_ISSUE_TYPE_FIELDS (requires projectIdOrKey and issueTypeId parameters) to discover available custom fields and their IDs - this is the recommended tool for creation-specific metadata. NOTE: The 'resolution' field cannot be set at issue creation - it can only be set during workflow transitions (e.g., when moving an issue to Done/Closed status). If 'resolution' is included, it will be automatically filtered out. IMPORTANT: Keys must use numeric IDs (e.g., 'customfield_10104'), NOT display names — using display names causes 400 Unknown field errors.
additional_properties.human_parameter_description: Extra fields to set on the issue as a JSON string. Use this for custom fields like Story Points or any project-specific fields. Use JIRA_GET_CREATE_METADATA_ISSUE_TYPE_FIELDS (requires projectIdOrKey and issueTypeId) to find field IDs - this is the recommended tool for getting creation-specific field metadata. query.human_parameter_description: Words to search for in the project name or key. Use part of a name or key to narrow the list.

action.title: ProjectAction

expand.title: Expand

status.title: Status

fields_by_keys.title: Fields By Keys

update_history.title: Update History

body.title: Body

is_html.title: Is Html

show_as.title: Show As

subject.title: Subject

user_id.title: User Id

user_id.human_parameter_description: The identifier of the user whose calendar the event will be created in. Use 'me' for your own calendar. For other users, provide their organizational email (Microsoft 365 work/school account) or Azure AD object ID. Do not use personal email addresses.

location.title: Location
location.description: The physical location of the event.

time_zone.title: Time Zone
time_zone.description: The time zone for the start and end times of the event. Uses Windows time zone names (e.g., 'Pacific Standard Time') or IANA time zone names (e.g., 'America/Los_Angeles'). UTC is also a valid input.
time_zone.human_parameter_description: The time zone to apply to the start and end times. Pick the zone that matches where the event is scheduled.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: A list of category names to associate with the event. The API accepts any string values. categories.human_parameter_description: Optional labels to organize the event. Any category name is accepted; for color-coding in Outlook, use categories from your mailbox's master list.

importance.title: Importance
importance.description: The importance of the event. Valid values are 'low', 'normal', 'high'. Defaults to 'normal'.
importance.human_parameter_description: How important this event is. Use 'high' to flag critical meetings or 'low' for optional ones.

is_all_day.title: Is All Day
is_all_day.description: Set to true for an all-day event. When true, start_datetime and end_datetime must both be at midnight and use the same time_zone.
is_all_day.human_parameter_description: Turn this on for an all-day event. Use midnight for both Start DateTime and End DateTime; the end is exclusive.

recurrence.title: PatternedRecurrence

range.title: RecurrenceRange

type.title: Type
type.description: The recurrence range. The possible values are: endDate, noEnd, numbered.

endDate.title: End Date
endDate.description: The date to stop applying the recurrence pattern. Depending on the recurrence pattern of the event, the last occurrence of the meeting may not be this date. Required if type is endDate.

startDate.title: Start Date
startDate.description: The date to start applying the recurrence pattern. The first occurrence of the meeting may be this date or later, depending on the recurrence pattern of the event. Must be the same value as the start property of the recurring event.

recurrenceTimeZone.title: Recurrence Time Zone
recurrenceTimeZone.description: Time zone for the startDate and endDate properties. Optional. If not specified, the time zone of the event is used.

numberOfOccurrences.title: Number Of Occurrences
numberOfOccurrences.description: The number of times to repeat the event. Required and must be positive if type is numbered.

range.description: The duration of a recurring event.

pattern.title: RecurrencePattern

type.title: Type
type.description: The recurrence pattern type: daily, weekly, absoluteMonthly, relativeMonthly, absoluteYearly, relativeYearly.

index.title: Index
index.description: Specifies on which instance of the allowed days specified in daysOfWeek the event occurs, counted from the first instance in the month. The possible values are: first, second, third, fourth, last. Default is first. Optional and used if type is relativeMonthly or relativeYearly.

month.title: Month
month.description: The month in which the event occurs. This is a number from 1 to 12.

interval.title: Interval
interval.description: The number of units between occurrences, where units can be in days, weeks, months, or years, depending on the type.

dayOfMonth.title: Day Of Month
dayOfMonth.description: The day of the month on which the event occurs. Required if type is absoluteMonthly or absoluteYearly.

daysOfWeek.title: Days Of Week
daysOfWeek.description: A collection of the days of the week on which the event occurs. The possible values are: sunday, monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday. If type is relativeMonthly or relativeYearly, and daysOfWeek specifies morethan one day, the event falls on the first day that satisfies the pattern. Required if type is weekly, relativeMonthly, or relativeYearly.

firstDayOfWeek.title: First Day Of Week
firstDayOfWeek.description: The first day of the week. The possible values are: sunday, monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday. Default is sunday. Required if type is weekly.

pattern.description: The frequency of a recurring event.

recurrence.description: The recurrence pattern and range for an event.
recurrence.human_parameter_description: Set up a recurring event pattern (daily, weekly, monthly, etc.) with how long it should repeat.

calendar_id.title: Calendar Id
calendar_id.description: The ID of a specific calendar to create the event in. Obtainable from the list calendars action. If omitted, the event is created on the user's default calendar.
calendar_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the calendar where you want to create the event. Leave blank to use your default calendar, or provide a calendar ID from the list of available calendars.

end_datetime.title: End Datetime
end_datetime.description: The event's end date and time. Prefer local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with the IANA or Windows zone in time_zone. Z or a numeric offset is accepted only when it agrees with time_zone.

attendees_info.title: Attendees Info

start_datetime.title: Start Datetime
start_datetime.description: The event's start date and time. Prefer local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with the IANA or Windows zone in time_zone. Z or a numeric offset is accepted only when it agrees with time_zone.
start_datetime.human_parameter_description: When the event starts. Enter the date and time; the Time Zone field decides how it’s interpreted.

is_online_meeting.title: Is Online Meeting

is_online_meeting.human_parameter_description: Turn this on to add an online meeting link to the event.

online_meeting_provider.title: Online Meeting Provider
online_meeting_provider.description: Specifies the online meeting provider. Currently, only 'teamsForBusiness' is supported. If 'is_online_meeting' is true and this is set, a meeting link for the provider will be created.
online_meeting_provider.human_parameter_description: Which service to use for the online meeting (for example, Microsoft Teams). Only set this if you’re creating an online meeting.

examples: name contains 'report' and not name contains 'draft'
name contains 'invoice' and modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00' and trashed = false
q.description:
Query string to filter file results. Accepts both simple text searches and full Google Drive query syntax.

        **Simple Text Search:** Bare text (e.g., "SAM RFP") is auto-converted to fullText search. Bare email addresses are auto-converted to owner search.

        **Full Query Syntax:** 'field operator value' combined with 'and', 'or', 'not'

        **Operators:** =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, contains, in

        **Common Fields:**
        - `name` - File name (exact match with = or partial match with contains)
        - `fullText` - File content search
        - `mimeType` - File type (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'application/vnd.google-apps.folder')
        - `modifiedTime`, `createdTime` - Dates (RFC 3339: '2024-01-01T00:00:00')
        - `parents` - Folder IDs containing the file
        - `owners`, `writers` - User email addresses (MUST use 'in' operator, NOT colon syntax)
        - `properties`, `appProperties` - Custom metadata

        **Boolean Filter Fields (sharedWithMe, trashed, starred):**
        These fields require explicit `= true` or `= false` syntax:
        - `sharedWithMe = true` - Find files shared with you by others
        - `sharedWithMe = false` - Find files NOT shared with you (your own files)
        - `trashed = true` - Find files in trash
        - `trashed = false` - Exclude trashed files from results
        - `starred = true` - Find starred/favorited files
        - `starred = false` - Find non-starred files

        Combine with other conditions using 'and':
        - "sharedWithMe = true and name contains 'report'" - Find shared files with 'report' in name
        - "sharedWithMe = true and mimeType = 'application/pdf'" - Find shared PDF files
        - "starred = true and modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00'" - Find recently modified starred files

        **Query Complexity Limits:**
        Queries with many OR clauses (typically >5-10) may fail with 'The query is too complex' error.

        **Name Field Usage:**
        Wildcards (*) are NOT supported. Use 'contains' operator for partial matching.

        **User Email Searches:**
        - CORRECT: "'user@example.com' in owners" or "'user@example.com' in writers" or "'user@example.com' in readers"
        - INCORRECT: "owner:user@example.com" (colon syntax is NOT supported and will cause errors)
        - Always use the 'in' operator with quoted email addresses for user-based searches

        **Special Syntax:**
        - Dates: RFC 3339 format (time zone defaults to UTC)
        - Apostrophes/quotes in values: Automatically escaped. You can write "name = 'Jan'26'" or "name = 'Valentine's Day'" without manual escaping.
        - Grouping: Use parentheses for OR: "(mimeType contains 'image/' or mimeType contains 'video/')"
        - Custom properties: "properties has { key='department' and value='sales' }"

        **IMPORTANT - Root Folder ('My Drive'):**
        'My Drive' is NOT a searchable folder name. To work with the root folder, use the 'root' alias: folder_id='root' or "'root' in parents" in your query.
q.human_parameter_description: Write a search filter to find the files you want, like name contains 'report' or modifiedTime > '2024-01-01'. Use this to narrow results to exactly what you need.

**Format:** For file fields, use 'files(field1,field2,...)' format. For example: 'files(id,name,mimeType)'.

Specifies which collections of files to search. Defaults to 'allDrives' (searches My Drive + all accessible shared drives).

        **Values:**
        - `user` - Search only user's personal My Drive
        - `domain` - Search all files shared within Google Workspace domain
        - `drive` - Search specific shared drive (requires 'driveId' parameter and 'includeItemsFromAllDrives' must be true)
        - `allDrives` - Search My Drive + all accessible shared drives (DEFAULT, requires 'includeItemsFromAllDrives' to be true)

        **When to Use:**
        - Personal files only: Use 'user'
        - Organization-wide: Use 'domain'
        - Specific shared drive: Use 'drive' with 'driveId'
        - Maximum coverage: Use 'allDrives' (auto-enables supportsAllDrives and includeItemsFromAllDrives)

query.description:
SQL-like query string to filter and retrieve Customer entities ONLY. Do NOT use for other entities (Invoice, Bill, Payment, etc.) - use their respective query tools. 

Query syntax: SELECT [fields] FROM Customer [WHERE conditions] [ORDER BY field] [STARTPOSITION n] [MAXRESULTS n] 

CRITICAL SYNTAX RESTRICTIONS: - Parentheses for grouping are NOT supported - OR operator is NOT supported - use IN instead - Use: WHERE Active = true AND DisplayName IN ('Customer A', 'Customer B') 

NOTE: QuickBooks API returns ALL fields regardless of SELECT clause. 

Commonly queryable fields: Id, DisplayName, CompanyName, FamilyName, GivenName, FullyQualifiedName, Active, Balance, PrimaryEmailAddr. 

Supports: - WHERE with operators (=, <, >, <=, >=, IN) - LIKE with % wildcard - AND only (no OR - use IN for multiple values) - ORDER BY for sorting (MUST be two words, not 'ORDERBY'). Sortable fields: DisplayName, FamilyName, GivenName, Id. - MAXRESULTS (max 1000, default 25) and STARTPOSITION - COUNT

NOTE: QuickBooks API returns ALL fields regardless of SELECT clause. 

Commonly queryable fields: Id, Name, Type, Active, Sku, Description, FullyQualifiedName, UnitPrice, PurchaseCost, QtyOnHand. 

NON-QUERYABLE fields: IncomeAccountRef, ExpenseAccountRef, AssetAccountRef, ParentRef, ClassRef. Using these in WHERE causes QueryValidationError.

b`. For Slack mentions, use explicit entity syntax such as <@USER_ID>, <#CHANNEL_ID>, or <!subteam^GROUP_ID>; do not rely on @name or #name auto-linking.
